name: Aquila
overview: Aquila was a male Jew native of Pontus who is noted in the New Testament as a companion of the Apostle Paul. He is recognized primarily for hosting Paul during his ministry, as recorded in Acts 18:2. Beyond this, the Scriptures provide limited additional details about his background or tribe.
namesAndTitles: The name Aquila appears only once in the biblical record and carries no specific meaning or divine origin noted in the text. It is simply presented as a proper name without further explanation.
familyAndRelationships: Scripture identifies Aquila as the husband of Priscilla, indicating a close partnership in ministry. No other family relationships are recorded beyond this marital connection.
scriptureSignificance: Aquila is significant in the biblical narrative as a faithful Jewish believer who supported Paul's mission by providing lodging and likely collaborating in ministry efforts. His partnership with Priscilla and Paul highlights the early church's reliance on committed believers who contributed to spreading the gospel. His presence in Acts 18:2 underscores the importance of hospitality and teamwork in advancing Christ-centered ministry.
